TASKS.wrong: Do not add 3 + 4; use Pythagoras for the diagonal.

steps.name: Read the signatures

steps.name: Through the origin
steps.narration: Graph B has the same gradient of two, but passes through zero zero. This is a direct proportion line.

steps.name: Negative gradient

steps.name: Straight against curved

steps.prompt: A straight line is not the same as a quadratic curve.

steps.name: Upward quadratic
steps.narration: The positive x-squared curve forms a U. Its lowest point is zero, negative one.
steps.prompt: The turning point is a minimum at (0, −1).

steps.name: Downward quadratic
steps.narration: The negative x-squared curve forms a hill. Its highest point is zero, five.
steps.prompt: The turning point is a maximum at (0, 5).

steps.name: Find useful crossings
steps.narration: A graph crossing the x axis shows where y equals zero. Graph C has roots one and three.

steps.name: Model a constant increase
steps.narration: A taxi starts at three pounds and costs two more for each mile. The constant rate creates a straight line.
steps.prompt: A fixed starting cost does not pass through (0,0).

steps.name: Model a changing rate
steps.narration: The height of the ball first increases and then decreases. A curved arch models the turn.
steps.prompt: Do not model a changing rate with a single straight line.

steps.name: Read two joined rules
steps.narration: Graph A rises to one, three, and then stays flat at three. The rule changes at the join.
steps.prompt: Check each interval independently.

steps.name: Spot a jump
steps.narration: The two parts of Graph B do not meet at x equals zero. A hollow point shows the first rule does not include the join.
steps.prompt: A graph can contain a discontinuity.

steps.name: Direct proportion
steps.narration: Direct proportion gives a straight line through zero zero. Double x and y doubles.
steps.prompt: A straight line alone is not enough for direct proportion.

steps.name: Inverse proportion

TASKS.q: How many HOURS does the walker rest at the café between hour 2 and hour 4?
TASKS.hint: Subtract the first time on the flat section from the last time.
TASKS.explain: 4 − 2 = 2 hours stopped. A flat distance–time section means zero speed.
TASKS.wrong: The flat line is at 6 km, but the question asks for its DURATION, not its height.

TASKS.q: From hour 0 to hour 2 the walker travels 6 km. What is the SPEED in km/h?
TASKS.hint: Speed = 6 km divided by 2 hours.
TASKS.explain: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 km/h. The gradient tells speed on this segment.
TASKS.wrong: The 6 km line height is distance, not speed. Divide by the elapsed time.

TASKS.q: From hour 4 to hour 6 the distance changes from 6 km to 10 km. What speed in km/h?
TASKS.hint: Change in distance is 10 − 6 = 4 km; elapsed time is 6 − 4 = 2 h.
TASKS.explain: 4 km in 2 h gives 2 km/h.
TASKS.wrong: Avoid using the final height of 10 km as the journey section distance.

TASKS.q: How many kilometres are travelled in TOTAL during the full journey?
TASKS.hint: The Y8 journey never turns towards home; add the distances on the rising sections.
TASKS.explain: 6 + 4 = 10 km travelled, with two stops along the way.
TASKS.wrong: Add only distance changes while moving, not durations of stationary periods.

TASKS.q: Between hours 3 and 5 the traveller moves FROM 8 km TO 2 km from home. What is their SPEED in km/h?
TASKS.hint: The distance from home FALLS by 6 km in 2 h. Speed is the positive magnitude.
TASKS.explain: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 km/h towards home. Gradient = −3 km/h, but speed = +3 km/h.
TASKS.wrong: A negative gradient shows return direction, NOT negative speed.

TASKS.q: Across the entire Year 9 journey, how far was travelled IN TOTAL?
TASKS.hint: Add all absolute vertical changes: first outward, return, then outward again.
TASKS.explain: Out 8 km + back 6 km + away 6 km = 20 km travelled.
TASKS.wrong: Do not use only the final graph height: it is distance FROM HOME, not the entire route length.

TASKS.q: At hour 8, how many kilometres is the traveller FROM HOME?
TASKS.hint: Read the graph height at x = 8 hours.
TASKS.explain: The final plotted point is (8 h, 8 km). The total travel distance is 20 km instead.
TASKS.wrong: The final y-coordinate is 8 km; total journey distance is a different quantity.

TASKS.q: How many HOURS are spent stopped on the Year 9 journey, added together?
TASKS.hint: There are two horizontal sections: 2 to 3 and 5 to 6.
TASKS.explain: 1 hour resting at 8 km + 1 hour resting at 2 km = 2 hours.
TASKS.wrong: Count time along the horizontal segments, not their kilometre heights.

TASKS.q: From 0 to 2 seconds velocity rises from 0 to 6 m/s. What is the ACCELERATION in m/s²?
TASKS.hint: Gradient = change in velocity ÷ change in time.
TASKS.explain: Acceleration = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 m/s².
TASKS.wrong: Six is the ending VELOCITY, not the acceleration. Divide by the two seconds.

TASKS.q: How far does the vehicle travel in the first 2 seconds? Give DISTANCE in metres.
TASKS.hint: Find the triangle area: half × 2 s × 6 m/s.
TASKS.explain: The triangle area is 6 metres, not 12. Area under a velocity–time graph is displacement.
TASKS.wrong: This is a triangle, not a rectangle: remember to take half the base times height.

TASKS.q: Between 2 and 4 seconds at 6 m/s, what DISTANCE does the vehicle cover in metres?
TASKS.hint: This region is a rectangle, 2 seconds wide and 6 m/s high.
TASKS.explain: 2 × 6 = 12 metres of steady travel.
TASKS.wrong: The graph is flat ABOVE zero. It means constant velocity, NOT zero distance.

TASKS.q: For the entire 8-second Year 8 graph, how far does the vehicle travel in metres?

TASKS.q: What is the acceleration from 4 s to 5 s when velocity changes from 6 m/s to 0?

TASKS.explain: Acceleration is −6 m/s². Velocity is still non-negative during this interval.
TASKS.wrong: The line slopes DOWN, so its gradient is negative; do not confuse this with the velocity sign.

TASKS.q: How many metres of FORWARD displacement are represented by all areas ABOVE zero?

TASKS.wrong: Above-zero area is forward displacement. Do not add the below-zero region here.

TASKS.q: What is the NET displacement after 8 seconds, in metres? Use a minus sign if needed.
TASKS.hint: Forward area is +21 m; backward area magnitude is 8 m.
TASKS.explain: 21 − 8 = +13 metres. Net displacement includes direction.
TASKS.wrong: Subtract the backward area. Do not add it as if you were asked for total distance.

TASKS.q: What is the TOTAL distance travelled after 8 seconds, in metres?
TASKS.hint: Add the MAGNITUDES of both shaded areas: 21 and 8.
TASKS.explain: 21 + 8 = 29 metres. Distance is always non-negative.
TASKS.wrong: For distance, add both forward and backward travel; 13 metres is net DISPLACEMENT.

TASKS.q: For y = x², what is the constant SECOND DIFFERENCE when x increases by 1?
TASKS.hint: Table: y is 4, 1, 0, 1, 4. Compare differences twice.
TASKS.wrong: First differences change. Find the differences of those differences.
TASKS.explain: First differences are −3, −1, 1, 3; second differences are all +2.

TASKS.q: What is the y-coordinate of the MINIMUM turning point?
TASKS.hint: Look at the bottom of the U-shaped curve.
TASKS.wrong: The lowest y-coordinate is negative.
TASKS.explain: The turning point is (1, −4), so its y-coordinate is −4.

TASKS.q: What is the LEFT-hand x-intercept (root) of this parabola?
TASKS.hint: Find where the curve crosses y = 0 on the left.
TASKS.wrong: The left root has a negative x-coordinate.
TASKS.explain: The roots are x = −1 and x = 3; the left root is −1.

TASKS.q: What is the RIGHT-hand x-intercept (root) of this downward parabola?
TASKS.hint: Read the right crossing of the horizontal axis.
TASKS.wrong: The roots are on either side of x = −1.
TASKS.explain: The roots are −3 and 1; the right-hand root is 1.

TASKS.q: What x-value gives the VERTICAL AXIS OF SYMMETRY?
TASKS.hint: The symmetry axis passes through the maximum.
TASKS.wrong: The axis is x = a constant, not a y-value.
TASKS.explain: The maximum is at x = −1, so the symmetry axis is x = −1.

TASKS.q: For the quadratic y = 0.5x² − 2, what is y when x = 2?
TASKS.hint: Square 2 first, multiply by one half, then subtract 2.
TASKS.wrong: Use the curved quadratic, not the comparison line.

TASKS.q: Estimate the RIGHT root of the quadratic graph.
TASKS.hint: Read where the curve meets y = 0 on the right.
TASKS.wrong: This is an x-coordinate, not the height of the vertex.
TASKS.explain: The roots are 0 and 4; the right root is 4.

TASKS.q: What is the x-coordinate of the turning point?
TASKS.hint: The turning point lies halfway between the two roots.
TASKS.wrong: Find the x-position where the curve turns.
TASKS.explain: Halfway between roots 0 and 4 is x = 2.

TASKS.q: How many REAL roots does this quadratic have?
TASKS.hint: Does the curve cross or touch the x-axis anywhere?
TASKS.wrong: A quadratic can have two, one or zero real roots.
TASKS.explain: The minimum is above y = 0, so it has zero real roots.

TASKS.q: For the QUADRATIC y = x² + 1, what is y when x = 2?
TASKS.hint: Use the curved quadratic, not the straight comparison line.
TASKS.wrong: The straight line gives another result. Square x for the quadratic.
TASKS.explain: 2² + 1 = 5. The straight comparison line gives 7, not 5.

TASKS.q: At the step change x = 3, which y value is INCLUDED?

TASKS.wrong: The open endpoint at y = two is excluded. Read the filled point at y = five.

TASKS.q: At x = 4, the upper point is open. What is the actual y value?

TASKS.wrong: An open point cannot count as the function value at the boundary.

TASKS.q: GCSE extension: at x = 4 which y value is included?
TASKS.hint: Compare hollow and solid endpoints at x = four.
TASKS.wrong: The open endpoint at y = six is not included: choose the solid endpoint.

TASKS.q: Read sin 0°. What is the output?
TASKS.hint: The sine graph starts on the horizontal axis.
TASKS.wrong: Sine starts at zero, not one.

TASKS.q: What is sin 90°?
TASKS.hint: Read the first peak at a quarter-turn.
TASKS.wrong: Sine reaches positive one at ninety degrees.

TASKS.q: What is sin 270°?
TASKS.hint: This is the trough below the x axis.
TASKS.wrong: The third-quarter-turn sine value is negative one.

TASKS.q: What is cos 0°?
TASKS.hint: Cosine starts at the top of the graph.
TASKS.wrong: Cosine starts at positive one; sine starts at zero.

TASKS.q: What is cos 180°?
TASKS.hint: Read the cosine trough at half a turn.
TASKS.wrong: Cosine at half a turn is minus one.

TASKS.q: What is tan 45°?
TASKS.hint: Sine and cosine have the same value at forty-five degrees.
TASKS.wrong: Tangent at forty-five degrees is positive one.

TASKS.q: What is tan 90°? Type “undefined”.
TASKS.hint: Cosine is zero here; division by zero is undefined.
TASKS.wrong: Tangent has a vertical asymptote and no value at ninety degrees.

TASKS.q: What is tan 180°?
TASKS.hint: The tangent branch crosses the horizontal axis here.
TASKS.wrong: Tangent is zero at a half-turn.

TASKS.q: What is the period of y = sin x in degrees?
TASKS.hint: One entire wave repeats after a complete turn.
TASKS.wrong: Sine repeats after three hundred and sixty degrees.

TASKS.q: What is the period of y = tan x in degrees?
TASKS.hint: Tangent repeats after a half-turn.
TASKS.wrong: Tangent repeats every one hundred and eighty degrees.

TASKS.q: For y = sin(2x), what is the period in degrees?
TASKS.hint: Two waves fit into one full turn. Divide three hundred and sixty by two.
TASKS.wrong: Doubling the angle halves the period to one hundred and eighty degrees.

TASKS.q: For y = 1.5 sin x, what is the amplitude?
TASKS.hint: Amplitude is the distance from the midline to a peak.
TASKS.wrong: Amplitude is one and a half; it is not the peak-to-trough distance.

TASKS.q: For the shifted cosine preset, what is its vertical shift?
TASKS.hint: Read the horizontal midline, not the maximum.
TASKS.wrong: The graph’s midline is raised by one half.
